analysis.investment_thesis: Optiemus is a thin-margin distribution business pivoting into electronics/drone manufacturing under the PLI narrative, but 9-year revenue CAGR of -0.2%, sub-15% ROE, and negative FCF of -96 Cr in FY25 offer no support for a 55.6x P/E. The Make-in-India manufacturing story here is real at the macro level but unproven at the company level, making the valuation a dangerous speculation.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 72.17% with manageable D/E of 0.32 — balance sheet not yet distressed
Revenue recovery is real: from 182 Cr (FY21) back to 1,890 Cr (FY25), showing operational resilience
CWIP of 99 Cr signals active manufacturing capacity build — positioned for PLI scheme benefits in electronics/drones
key_risks: Valuation is absurd at 55.6x P/E and EV/EBITDA of 33x for a 5.28% operating margin distribution business — priced for perfection that doesn't exist
FCF deeply negative at -96 Cr in FY25 and OCF turned negative (-13 Cr) — business is a cash consumer, not a cash generator
9-year revenue CAGR of -0.2% exposes chronic execution failure; the 2021 'profit' of 95 Cr was non-operational (other income 206 Cr vs -93 Cr EBITDA) — quality of earnings is poor
red_flags: Net profit CAGR of 19.2% is a statistical illusion — FY21 base profitability was entirely driven by 206 Cr exceptional other income, not operations
Finance costs exploded from 5 Cr (FY21) to 30 Cr (FY25) as borrowings rose from 43 to 247 Cr — leverage is quietly building as FCF bleeds
ROE of only 11.6% falls below my minimum 15% threshold for any serious consideration — capital is being destroyed at current valuations
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Optiemus Infracom is fundamentally a mobile handset and accessories distributor that lost its way badly through FY18-FY21 (revenue collapsed from 1,922 Cr to 182 Cr) and is now re-inventing itself as a manufacturer of hearables, IT hardware, and drones. The recovery in revenue to 1,890 Cr in FY25 looks impressive on a chart, but it's barely back to 2016 levels after nine years — a -0.2% CAGR. At 5.28% operating margins with an ROE of 11.6% and ROCE of 14.4%, this is not the kind of business I want to own at any premium, let alone at 55.6x earnings. The market is paying a technology-manufacturing multiple for what is still predominantly a distribution business.

The manufacturing pivot via CWIP (99 Cr in FY25 vs near-zero before) and the drone narrative may be exciting for traders, but as an investor I look at cash flows — and they tell a grim story. FCF was -96 Cr in FY25, OCF turned negative at -13 Cr, and borrowings are quietly rising (247 Cr). The business is consuming capital faster than it generates returns. For me to get excited, I need to see consistent 15%+ ROE, double-digit revenue CAGR with margin expansion, and positive FCF. Optiemus has none of these at the moment. The India electronics manufacturing opportunity is real, but Dixon Technologies is executing it far better at similar or better valuations — I see no reason to bet on this weaker horse.
